subtopics.title: Whole-number operations and long division
subtopics.blurb: Add, subtract, multiply and long-divide whole numbers by hand, write remainders in the form asked, and check every answer.

subtopics.title: Order of operations
subtopics.blurb: Evaluate any expression in the agreed order: grouping, exponents, then multiplication and division and addition and subtraction, left to right where ranks tie.

subtopics.title: Integers, factors, multiples, primes, squares and roots
subtopics.blurb: Work with negative numbers, find factors, multiples, primes, the GCF and the LCM, and use perfect squares to find and estimate square roots.

subtopics.title: Place value and rounding
subtopics.blurb: Name every place from millions to ten-thousandths, read and write decimals in words, and round to any place correctly.

subtopics.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
subtopics.blurb: Add and subtract decimals by hand with the points lined up, empty places filled with zeros, and every borrow done correctly.

subtopics.title: Multiplying and dividing decimals
subtopics.blurb: Multiply decimals by counting decimal places, divide by moving the point until the divisor is whole, and shift the point for powers of 10.

subtopics.title: Multi-step word problems and estimation
subtopics.blurb: Solve one- and two-step money, rate, supply and dosage word problems at exam pace, and estimate to check the answer.

subtopics.title: Equivalent fractions, simplest form, mixed numbers and improper fractions
subtopics.blurb: Build equivalent fractions, switch between mixed numbers and improper fractions, and give every answer in the form asked: lowest terms or a mixed number.

subtopics.title: Comparing and ordering fractions and decimals
subtopics.blurb: Find the greatest, the least or the right order in any mix of fractions, mixed numbers and decimals, and read the direction the question asks for.

subtopics.title: Adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers
subtopics.blurb: Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers by hand with the least common denominator, carrying and borrowing without the slips the HESI A2 sets.

subtopics.title: Multiplying and dividing fractions and mixed numbers
subtopics.blurb: Multiply and divide fractions and mixed numbers by hand: convert to improper fractions first, cross-cancel, and multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.

subtopics.title: Converting fractions, decimals and percents
subtopics.blurb: Switch any value between fraction, decimal and percent form quickly and without decimal-point slips.

subtopics.title: Percent of a number, what percent, and finding the whole
subtopics.blurb: Use part = percent × whole to find a part, a percent or a whole, and convert percents to decimals without slipping a place.

subtopics.title: Percent increase and decrease, discount, tax and tip
subtopics.blurb: Find percent increase and decrease from the right base, price discounts, tax, tips and markups with multipliers, and undo a percent correctly.

subtopics.title: Fraction and percent word problems
subtopics.blurb: Solve one- and two-step fraction and percent word problems: decide what each fraction or percent is taken of, and answer the exact question asked.

subtopics.title: Ratios: part-to-part and part-to-whole
subtopics.blurb: Write and simplify ratios in the right order, turn part-to-part ratios into fractions of the whole, and share or change amounts in a ratio.

subtopics.title: Unit rates and rate problems
subtopics.blurb: Find unit rates and better buys, convert hours and minutes before you divide, and use a rate to find an amount, a time or an average speed.

subtopics.title: Solving proportions by cross-multiplication
subtopics.blurb: Set up a proportion with matching units in matching places, solve it by cross-multiplying, and spot when a relationship is inverse instead.

subtopics.title: Dosage-style proportion problems: desired over have
subtopics.blurb: Use desired ÷ have × quantity to find tablets and milliliters from the facts in the stem, after matching units and converting pounds to kilograms.

subtopics.title: Evaluating expressions and translating words into algebra
subtopics.blurb: Turn word phrases into algebraic expressions without reversing the order, then evaluate them in real-world settings.

subtopics.title: Solving one-variable equations
subtopics.blurb: Solve one-variable equations by undoing operations, distributing, clearing fractions and decimals, and collecting the variable on one side, then check.

subtopics.title: Algebra word problems
subtopics.blurb: Turn a short story into one equation: name the unknown, translate each phrase, solve, and answer the exact question asked.

subtopics.title: Household measures: teaspoons to gallons
subtopics.blurb: Convert teaspoons, tablespoons, fluid ounces, cups, pints, quarts and gallons in either direction, and handle the customary length and weight units that support them.

subtopics.title: Household-to-metric conversions
subtopics.blurb: Turn teaspoons, tablespoons and fluid ounces into milliliters from memory, use the cup, pint, quart and gallon values a question gives you, and work out how long a supply lasts.

subtopics.title: Pounds and kilograms, inches and centimeters
subtopics.blurb: Change pounds to kilograms and back with 2.2, inches to centimeters and back with 2.54, and handle heights and weights written in mixed units.

subtopics.title: Metric prefixes and conversions
subtopics.blurb: Read any metric prefix, slide between units by powers of 10, and convert doses, volumes and lengths without a decimal slip.

subtopics.title: Multi-step conversions with dimensional analysis
subtopics.blurb: Chain unit fractions so the units cancel step by step, and solve two- and three-step conversions across household, metric, weight and time units without guessing which way to go.

subtopics.title: Fahrenheit and Celsius
subtopics.blurb: Convert any temperature between Celsius and Fahrenheit with the steps in the right order, compare readings on different scales, and convert a change in temperature.

subtopics.title: Roman numerals
subtopics.blurb: Read and write Roman numerals up to 3,999 with the seven symbols, the six subtractive pairs and the three-in-a-row rule, and do arithmetic by converting first.

subtopics.title: Military (24-hour) time
subtopics.blurb: Convert between standard a.m./p.m. time and four-digit military time in both directions, including the noon and midnight hours, and put times from a whole day in order.

subtopics.title: Elapsed time, including across midnight
subtopics.blurb: Find the time between two clock readings, add or subtract a duration, cross midnight without losing a day, and switch between minutes, hours and decimal hours.

subtopics.title: Working a health passage under time
subtopics.blurb: Work a 250-500 word health passage and its question set at HESI pace: skim for gists, classify each stem, scan for key words and match every qualifier.

subtopics.title: Topic vs main idea
subtopics.blurb: Tell the topic from the main idea, find the sentence that states the main idea of a multi-paragraph passage, and reject options that are too narrow or too broad.

subtopics.title: Implied main ideas and the best title
subtopics.blurb: Build the main idea when no sentence states it, and choose the title that names the topic and reflects that idea without being too broad or too narrow.

subtopics.title: Supporting details and locating facts
subtopics.blurb: Tell major from minor details, pick the detail that really supports a claim, and find stated facts with every qualifier matched.

subtopics.title: Choosing the best summary
subtopics.blurb: Pick the summary that covers every paragraph, in order, with the right emphasis and nothing added.

subtopics.title: Sequence and organizational patterns
subtopics.blurb: Rebuild the true order of events and name a passage's organizational pattern from how its ideas connect, not from one signal word.

subtopics.title: Word meaning in context
subtopics.blurb: Answer 'As used in paragraph 2, the word ___ most nearly means' items using context clues, the right sense of a multiple-meaning word and plain readings of figurative phrases.

subtopics.title: Tone and the author's attitude
subtopics.blurb: Separate a word's dictionary meaning from the feeling it carries, and use word choice to name an author's tone precisely.

subtopics.title: Inferences: what the passage implies
subtopics.blurb: Read between the lines: combine clues from across a passage with reasoning to find what it most strongly implies.

subtopics.title: Inference vs outside knowledge and overreach
subtopics.blurb: Separate what a passage supports from what a reader assumes, and reject options that are true in real life but not in the text.

subtopics.title: Drawing logical conclusions
subtopics.blurb: Combine a passage's details into the conclusion it best supports, and reject conclusions that claim more than the evidence shows.

subtopics.title: Health and science passages: claims, numbers, cause and effect
subtopics.blurb: Read health and science passages exactly: match every number to its group, follow cause and effect, and separate what was found from what was proved.

subtopics.title: Author's purpose
subtopics.blurb: Decide why an author wrote a whole text, or included one paragraph or statistic, even when facts are used to persuade.

subtopics.title: Fact vs opinion
subtopics.blurb: Sort any sentence into fact or opinion with one test, including the tricky ones with numbers, experts and mixed claims.

subtopics.title: Putting it together: a full passage set
subtopics.blurb: Work a whole HESI passage set at exam pace: one careful read, paragraph gists, then main idea, detail and inference items answered from the right place.

subtopics.title: Signs and symptoms words
subtopics.blurb: Name the exact meaning of the fever, color, breathing, dizziness and wound words the HESI A2 pairs as traps.

subtopics.title: Onset, severity and course words
subtopics.blurb: Define the words for how an illness starts, flares, fades, returns and ends, and avoid the paired-opposite traps.

subtopics.title: Infection, hygiene and safety words
subtopics.blurb: Define the words for germs, spread, outbreaks, harm and protection, and keep sterile, aseptic and septic apart.

subtopics.title: Assessment and observation words
subtopics.blurb: Define the words for examining, measuring and observing a patient, from auscultate and palpate to patent, occult and lucid.

subtopics.title: Treatment and care words
subtopics.blurb: Know the HESI A2 words for the goal of care, procedures and recovery, and never mix up palliative and prophylactic or incision and excision.

subtopics.title: Medication and route words
subtopics.blurb: Read the HESI A2 words for why a drug is given, how it gets into the body and what it does, and beat the prescribe/proscribe and adverse/averse traps.

subtopics.title: Patient behavior and communication words
subtopics.blurb: Describe how a patient acts, feels and communicates in HESI A2 words, and keep compliant, complacent, apathy and empathy apart.

subtopics.title: Body position and direction words
subtopics.blurb: Read the HESI A2 words for lying positions, body directions, sides and limb movements, and stop reversing supine/prone, proximal/distal and abduct/adduct.

subtopics.title: Body process words
subtopics.blurb: Name what the body is doing in HESI A2 words, from ingest to excrete, and never swap excrete/secrete, dilate/dilute or aspirate/expectorate.

subtopics.title: Context clues, synonyms and antonyms
subtopics.blurb: Work out an unfamiliar word from the one sentence around it, pick synonyms and antonyms in the right sense, and choose the meaning a multiple-meaning word has in context.

subtopics.title: Prefixes: number, size, position and negation
subtopics.blurb: Read the HESI A2 prefixes for number, size, position and negation, and keep hypo/hyper, inter/intra and ante/anti apart.

subtopics.title: Medical roots and suffixes
subtopics.blurb: Decode medical terms from their roots and suffixes, reading suffix first, use general roots (dict, port, tract) and word-form suffixes, and separate the look-alike endings the HESI A2 tests.

subtopics.title: General words for change, amount and degree
subtopics.blurb: Know the HESI A2 words for going up, going down and how much (abate, augment, deplete, negligible, copious) and dodge their look-alikes.

subtopics.title: General words for attitude and behavior
subtopics.blurb: Read the HESI A2 words that describe how people act and feel (diligent, complacent, ambivalent, prudent) and avoid their look-alikes.

subtopics.title: General words for thinking and communicating
subtopics.blurb: Master the HESI A2 words for understanding, explaining and reasoning (infer, imply, concise, explicit, corroborate) and their look-alike traps.

subtopics.title: General words for time, quality and condition
subtopics.blurb: Place the HESI A2 time words in order (prior, interim, subsequent), tell concurrent from consecutive, and read condition words such as intact, viable and adequate.

subtopics.title: The eight parts of speech
subtopics.blurb: Name the part of speech of any word by the job it does in the sentence, including words that switch jobs.

subtopics.title: Pronoun case: I or me, who or whom
subtopics.blurb: Choose I or me, we or us, who or whom, and myself only when it belongs, using two quick tests.

subtopics.title: Clear pronoun reference
subtopics.blurb: Spot pronouns that point two ways, point nowhere or point to a whole idea, and rewrite them so only one reading is possible.

subtopics.title: Verb tenses and tense consistency
subtopics.blurb: Keep tenses consistent, choose the perfect and progressive tenses for the right timing, and handle “if” sentences and active voice.

subtopics.title: Irregular verbs; lie and lay, sit and set, rise and raise
subtopics.blurb: Use the right past and past participle of common irregular verbs, and never mix up lie and lay, sit and set, or rise and raise.

subtopics.title: Adjectives and adverbs; good and well; comparisons
subtopics.blurb: Choose adjective or adverb (good or well, bad or badly, real or really) and form comparatives and superlatives correctly.

subtopics.title: Double negatives and nonstandard forms
subtopics.blurb: Spot double negatives (including hidden ones like hardly), nonstandard forms such as could of and irregardless, and the a/an choice.

subtopics.title: Commonly confused words: affect and effect, than and then, accept and except
subtopics.blurb: Choose the right word every time between their/there/they're, its/it's, affect/effect, than/then and the other high-yield pairs.

subtopics.title: Fewer and less, among and between, and other usage pairs
subtopics.blurb: Choose fewer or less, number or amount, imply or infer, who or which, and other usage pairs by what the word must mean in the sentence.

subtopics.title: Subject-verb agreement
subtopics.blurb: Find the true subject in any sentence and match the verb to it, even past phrases, pronouns like each, either/or pairs and inverted order.

subtopics.title: Pronoun-antecedent agreement
subtopics.blurb: Make every pronoun match its antecedent in number and person, including compound antecedents, things and organizations.

subtopics.title: Fragments, run-ons and comma splices
subtopics.blurb: Spot an incomplete sentence or two sentences jammed together, and fix it with one of the five correct joins.

subtopics.title: Misplaced modifiers and parallel structure
subtopics.blurb: Fix misplaced, dangling and limiting modifiers, and make lists, pairs, comparisons and correlative pairs parallel.

subtopics.title: Prepositions and idioms
subtopics.blurb: Choose at, on or in for times and places, tell in from into and since from for, and use the standard preposition after verbs and adjectives.

subtopics.title: Commas
subtopics.blurb: Place every required comma and remove every wrong one: FANBOYS, introductions, nonessential elements, series, adjectives, dates and addresses.

subtopics.title: Semicolons, colons, hyphens, parentheses, dashes and ellipses
subtopics.blurb: Use semicolons and colons only where a full sentence allows them, hyphenate compound modifiers, and handle dashes, parentheses and ellipses correctly.

subtopics.title: Apostrophes, quotation marks and dialogue
subtopics.blurb: Form singular, plural and joint possessives, place marks around quotation marks the American way, and punctuate dialogue tags.

subtopics.title: Capitalization
subtopics.blurb: Capitalize proper nouns, titles before names, regions, languages and the major words of titles, and leave common nouns lowercase.

subtopics.title: Levels of organization and the cell
subtopics.blurb: Put the six levels of body organization in order and classify any structure as a molecule, cell, tissue, organ or organ system.

subtopics.title: The four tissue types and body membranes
subtopics.blurb: Identify the four tissue types from their features, name epithelia by layer and shape, tell exocrine from endocrine glands, and match the four body membranes to where they lie.

subtopics.title: Anatomical position and directional terms
subtopics.blurb: Describe the anatomical position and use each pair of directional terms correctly, including the limb and forearm cases the exam loves.

subtopics.title: Body planes, cavities, quadrants and regions
subtopics.blurb: Name the plane behind any section, place organs in the correct body cavity, and locate structures by abdominal quadrant, region and regional term.

subtopics.title: Building anatomical terms from word parts
subtopics.blurb: Decode anatomical names from their position prefixes and structure roots, so you can place a structure such as the pericardium or an intercostal muscle without memorizing it.

subtopics.title: Homeostasis and feedback loops
subtopics.blurb: Name the parts of a feedback loop and classify any body response as negative or positive feedback from what it does to the original change.

subtopics.title: Heart chambers, valves and layers
subtopics.blurb: Name the four chambers, four valves and the layers of the heart wall, and explain the "lub" and "dub".

subtopics.title: Blood flow through the heart and the circulations
subtopics.blurb: Put every chamber, valve and great vessel in order, and explain why pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

subtopics.title: Conduction system, cardiac cycle and blood pressure
subtopics.blurb: Order the conduction pathway, read the P, QRS and T waves, and work out cardiac output and blood pressure.

subtopics.title: Blood vessels and blood
subtopics.blurb: Compare arteries, capillaries and veins, name every component of blood, and match ABO and Rh blood types.

subtopics.title: The respiratory tract
subtopics.blurb: Trace inhaled air from the nose to the alveoli and say what each structure does along the way.

subtopics.title: Breathing and gas exchange
subtopics.blurb: Explain how pressure changes move air in and out, how lung volumes add up, and how O₂ and CO₂ cross the respiratory membrane and travel in the blood.

subtopics.title: The lymphatic system and innate immunity
subtopics.blurb: Sort any defense into the first or second line, explain the steps of inflammation, and describe how lymph is collected, filtered and returned to the blood.

subtopics.title: Adaptive immunity, antibodies and vaccines
subtopics.blurb: Compare B and T cells, match each antibody class to its job, explain primary versus secondary responses, and classify immunity as active or passive, natural or artificial.

subtopics.title: Divisions of the nervous system
subtopics.blurb: Sort any nerve, signal or body response into CNS or PNS, sensory or motor, somatic or autonomic, sympathetic or parasympathetic.

subtopics.title: Neurons, impulses and synapses
subtopics.blurb: Trace a nerve impulse from dendrite to synapse: the parts of a neuron, myelin, the ion movements of an action potential and how neurotransmitters cross the gap.

subtopics.title: Brain, spinal cord, nerves and reflexes
subtopics.blurb: Match each brain region to its job, layer the meninges, read the spinal cord's roots and sequence a reflex arc.

subtopics.title: The special senses
subtopics.blurb: Follow light through the eye and sound through the ear in the right order, tell rods from cones and hearing from balance.

subtopics.title: Endocrine glands and their hormones
subtopics.blurb: Match each endocrine gland to its hormones and actions, tell steroid from peptide hormones, and recognize the classic hormone disorders.

subtopics.title: Hormone feedback: glucose, calcium, water and stress
subtopics.blurb: Predict which hormone the body releases when glucose, calcium or water balance drifts, and how the stress hormones take over in an emergency.

subtopics.title: The digestive tract in order
subtopics.blurb: Trace food from mouth to anus, name every segment in order, and say what each region does.

subtopics.title: Liver, gallbladder, pancreas and salivary glands
subtopics.blurb: Know what each accessory organ makes, where its secretion goes and which hormone releases it.

subtopics.title: Chemical digestion, enzymes and absorption
subtopics.blurb: Match each nutrient to where its digestion starts, the enzymes that split it, its end products and where they are absorbed.

subtopics.title: Kidneys, nephrons and urine formation
subtopics.blurb: Name every structure urine and filtrate pass through, in order, locate the parts of the kidney and nephron, and say what filtration, reabsorption and secretion do in each segment.

subtopics.title: Fluid, electrolyte and acid-base balance
subtopics.blurb: Place body water in its compartments, match Na⁺, K⁺ and Ca²⁺ to their jobs, predict what ADH, aldosterone, RAAS and ANP do, and explain how buffers, lungs and kidneys hold blood pH at 7.35–7.45.

subtopics.title: Male reproductive system
subtopics.blurb: Trace sperm from the seminiferous tubules to the urethra, match each gland and cell to its job, and explain how FSH, LH and testosterone control the testes.

subtopics.title: Female reproductive system and the menstrual cycle
subtopics.blurb: Follow the oocyte from ovary to uterus, link each phase of the 28-day cycle to its hormones, and explain hCG, oxytocin and prolactin in pregnancy and lactation.

subtopics.title: Fertilization, pregnancy and early development
subtopics.blurb: Trace a zygote to a fetus stage by stage, match each germ layer to what it builds, and explain hCG, the placenta, the umbilical vessels and the oxytocin loop of labor.

subtopics.title: Bone tissue, bone cells and growth
subtopics.blurb: Label a long bone, tell compact from spongy bone, name the bone cells and explain how bone grows, remodels and heals.

subtopics.title: The skeleton and joints
subtopics.blurb: Sort bones into axial and appendicular, count vertebrae and ribs, and match every joint type to its movement and example.

subtopics.title: Muscle types and major muscles
subtopics.blurb: Tell skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle apart, name agonist, antagonist, origin and insertion, and match major muscles to their actions.

subtopics.title: Skeletal muscle contraction
subtopics.blurb: Order the events from nerve signal to power stroke, explain the roles of calcium and ATP, and match energy systems and contraction types to real activity.

subtopics.title: Skin layers, glands and functions
subtopics.blurb: Order the epidermal layers, tell the dermis from the hypodermis, match each gland to its secretion and explain what skin does.

subtopics.title: Characteristics of life and classification
subtopics.blurb: Name the characteristics of living things, order the levels of organization, and classify organisms by domain, kingdom and binomial name.

subtopics.title: Natural selection and adaptation
subtopics.blurb: Explain how natural selection changes a population, tell it apart from drift, gene flow and Lamarck's rejected idea, and read the evidence for evolution.

subtopics.title: Properties of water
subtopics.blurb: Explain how water's polarity and hydrogen bonds produce cohesion, adhesion, high specific heat, evaporative cooling, floating ice and its power as a solvent.

subtopics.title: Carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and nucleic acids
subtopics.blurb: Identify the four macromolecules by monomer, bond, elements and function, and explain how enzymes work and what slows them down.

subtopics.title: Enzymes, ATP and metabolism
subtopics.blurb: Sort reactions into anabolism and catabolism, explain how ATP carries energy, and predict how temperature, pH, substrate and inhibitors change an enzyme's rate.

subtopics.title: Cell types and organelles
subtopics.blurb: Tell prokaryotic from eukaryotic and plant from animal cells, match every organelle to its job, trace a secreted protein, and explain how cells differentiate.

subtopics.title: The cell membrane and transport
subtopics.blurb: Explain how substances cross the cell membrane and predict what hypertonic, hypotonic and isotonic solutions do to cells.

subtopics.title: The cell cycle, mitosis and meiosis
subtopics.blurb: Order the cell cycle and the stages of mitosis, contrast mitosis with meiosis, and explain where genetic variation and nondisjunction come from.

subtopics.title: Cellular respiration
subtopics.blurb: Trace glucose through glycolysis, the Krebs cycle and the electron transport chain, with the location, inputs and outputs of each stage, and explain fermentation.

subtopics.title: Photosynthesis
subtopics.blurb: Write the photosynthesis equation, contrast the light-dependent reactions with the Calvin cycle by location, inputs and outputs, and explain where the oxygen comes from.

subtopics.title: DNA, RNA, protein synthesis and mutation
subtopics.blurb: Describe DNA and RNA, apply base pairing, follow replication, transcription and translation codon by codon, and classify mutations by their effect.

subtopics.title: Mendelian genetics and Punnett squares
subtopics.blurb: Use the language of genetics, state Mendel's laws, solve Punnett squares and probability questions, and handle incomplete dominance, codominance, ABO blood types and X-linked traits.

subtopics.title: States and properties of matter; physical and chemical change
subtopics.blurb: Classify matter, describe the states and phase changes, tell physical from chemical changes, calculate density and apply the basic gas laws.

subtopics.title: Atomic structure, isotopes and ions
subtopics.blurb: Count the protons, neutrons and electrons in any atom or ion, and tell isotopes from ions at a glance.

subtopics.title: The periodic table and periodic trends
subtopics.blurb: Read periods, groups, shells and valence electrons from the table, name the main families and predict radius, ionization energy, electronegativity and reactivity from position.

subtopics.title: Nuclear chemistry: decay and half-life
subtopics.blurb: Predict the product of alpha, beta and gamma decay, work half-life problems by hand and tell fission from fusion.

subtopics.title: Ionic, covalent, hydrogen and metallic bonds
subtopics.blurb: Predict the bond type from the elements involved, tell polar from nonpolar sharing and explain what hydrogen bonds do for water and DNA.

subtopics.title: Writing and balancing chemical equations
subtopics.blurb: Count atoms in any formula, write equations from words and balance them with coefficients, never subscripts.

subtopics.title: Reaction types, including oxidation-reduction
subtopics.blurb: Classify synthesis, decomposition, replacement, combustion and neutralization reactions, and find what is oxidized, what is reduced and which agent does each.

subtopics.title: Reaction rates, catalysts, energy and equilibrium
subtopics.blurb: Use collision theory to predict what speeds up or slows a reaction, read an energy diagram and apply Le Chatelier's principle.

subtopics.title: The mole, molar mass and simple stoichiometry
subtopics.blurb: Calculate molar mass, convert between grams, moles and particles by hand, and use a balanced equation's mole ratio to find how much product forms.

subtopics.title: Solutions and concentration
subtopics.blurb: Name solute and solvent, calculate molarity, percent and dilutions, and predict how temperature, pressure and dissolved particles change a solution.

subtopics.title: Acids, bases and pH
subtopics.blurb: Define acids and bases, use the logarithmic pH scale, tell strong from concentrated and explain how buffers hold blood pH between 7.35 and 7.45.

subtopics.title: Speed, velocity and acceleration
subtopics.blurb: Tell scalars from vectors, calculate speed, velocity and acceleration with the right units, and read position-time and velocity-time graphs.

subtopics.title: Free fall and projectile motion
subtopics.blurb: Calculate the speed and distance of a falling object, explain why mass does not matter, and split a projectile into its horizontal and vertical motions.

subtopics.title: Newton's laws, weight and friction
subtopics.blurb: Apply Newton's three laws, use F = ma with the net force, separate mass from weight, and calculate friction from the normal force.

subtopics.title: Momentum, impulse and collisions
subtopics.blurb: Calculate momentum and impulse, explain how air bags lower the force of a crash, and use conservation of momentum for collisions and recoil.

subtopics.title: Circular motion, rotation and gravitation
subtopics.blurb: Explain centripetal acceleration and force, calculate torque, period and frequency, and apply the inverse-square law of gravitation.

subtopics.title: Work, energy, power and conservation
subtopics.blurb: Calculate work, kinetic and potential energy and power, apply conservation of energy, and explain efficiency, simple machines and the three lever classes.

subtopics.title: Density, pressure and buoyancy
subtopics.blurb: Use density to predict floating and sinking, calculate pressure from force and area and from depth, and apply Pascal's and Archimedes' principles.

subtopics.title: Waves and sound
subtopics.blurb: Describe transverse and longitudinal waves, use v = fλ and f = 1/T, and explain sound speed, pitch, loudness, decibels, echoes, ultrasound and the Doppler effect.

subtopics.title: Light, mirrors, lenses and refraction
subtopics.blurb: Order the electromagnetic spectrum, apply the law of reflection, describe plane, concave and convex mirror images, and explain refraction, total internal reflection and corrective lenses.

subtopics.title: Charge, current, voltage, resistance and circuits
subtopics.blurb: Explain static charge, Coulomb's law and electric fields, then use Ohm's law, series and parallel rules and P = IV to solve circuit problems.

subtopics.title: Magnetism and electromagnetism
subtopics.blurb: Predict how magnetic poles interact, name ferromagnetic materials, strengthen an electromagnet, and explain motors, generators, transformers and induction.
